question: How many students are there?
gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM students

question: List the names of all departments.
gold_sql: SELECT name FROM departments

question: How many students are in their 2nd year of study?
gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM students WHERE year_of_study = 2

question: List the first and last names of students who live in Tokyo.
gold_sql: SELECT first_name, last_name FROM students WHERE city = 'Tokyo'

question: What is the highest score recorded in the marks table?
gold_sql: SELECT MAX(score) FROM marks

question: List the code and title of every course taught in the Spring semester.
gold_sql: SELECT code, title FROM courses WHERE semester = 'Spring'

question: How many courses are worth 4 credits?
gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM courses WHERE credits = 4

question: List all course titles ordered by credits from highest to lowest, breaking ties by title alphabetically.
gold_sql: SELECT title FROM courses ORDER BY credits DESC, title ASC

question: What is the average score across all graded marks, rounded to 2 decimal places?
gold_sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(score), 2) FROM marks

question: List the first names of female students in year 4.
gold_sql: SELECT first_name FROM students WHERE gender = 'F' AND year_of_study = 4

question: How many different cities do students come from?
gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT city) FROM students

question: What are the codes of the courses taught by Dr. Lena Novak?
gold_sql: SELECT code FROM courses WHERE instructor = 'Dr. Lena Novak'

question: List the first and last names of students who have not provided an email address.
gold_sql: SELECT first_name, last_name FROM students WHERE email IS NULL

question: Show the first and last names of the 5 youngest students, youngest first.
gold_sql: SELECT first_name, last_name FROM students ORDER BY date_of_birth DESC LIMIT 5

question: How many marks have a score of 90 or more?
gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM marks WHERE score >= 90

question: For each department name, how many students belong to it?
gold_sql: SELECT d.name, COUNT(s.student_id) FROM departments d JOIN students s ON s.dept_id = d.dept_id GROUP BY d.dept_id, d.name

question: List every course title together with the name of the department that offers it.
gold_sql: SELECT c.title, d.name FROM courses c JOIN departments d ON d.dept_id = c.dept_id

question: What is the average score for each course? Show the course code and the average rounded to 2 decimal places.
gold_sql: SELECT c.code, ROUND(AVG(m.score), 2) FROM courses c JOIN marks m ON m.course_id = c.course_id GROUP BY c.course_id, c.code

question: List the first and last names of students enrolled in the course titled 'Databases'.
gold_sql: SELECT s.first_name, s.last_name FROM students s JOIN marks m ON m.student_id = s.student_id JOIN courses c ON c.course_id = m.course_id WHERE c.title = 'Databases'

question: Show each course code with the number of students enrolled in it, including courses with no students.
gold_sql: SELECT c.code, COUNT(m.mark_id) FROM courses c LEFT JOIN marks m ON m.course_id = c.course_id GROUP BY c.course_id, c.code

question: Which cities have more than 6 students? Show the city and its number of students.
gold_sql: SELECT city, COUNT(*) FROM students GROUP BY city HAVING COUNT(*) > 6

question: List each department name with the number of courses it offers, ordered by the number of courses from most to fewest and then by department name alphabetically.
gold_sql: SELECT d.name, COUNT(c.course_id) AS n FROM departments d LEFT JOIN courses c ON c.dept_id = d.dept_id GROUP BY d.dept_id, d.name ORDER BY n DESC, d.name ASC

question: What is the average score of marks earned by students in the Computer Science department, rounded to 2 decimal places?
gold_sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(m.score), 2) FROM marks m JOIN students s ON s.student_id = m.student_id JOIN departments d ON d.dept_id = s.dept_id WHERE d.name = 'Computer Science'

question: Which instructors teach more than one course?
gold_sql: SELECT instructor FROM courses GROUP BY instructor HAVING COUNT(*) > 1

question: List the first and last names of students who scored above 90 in at least one course. Each student should appear once.
gold_sql: SELECT s.first_name, s.last_name FROM students s WHERE s.student_id IN (SELECT student_id FROM marks WHERE score > 90)

question: For each year of study, what is the average score of the marks earned by students in that year? Show the year and the average rounded to 2 decimal places.
gold_sql: SELECT s.year_of_study, ROUND(AVG(m.score), 2) FROM students s JOIN marks m ON m.student_id = s.student_id GROUP BY s.year_of_study

question: For each student who is enrolled in at least one course, show their student_id and the total number of credits of the courses they are enrolled in.
gold_sql: SELECT m.student_id, SUM(c.credits) FROM marks m JOIN courses c ON c.course_id = m.course_id GROUP BY m.student_id

question: How many exams took place in December 2025?
gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM marks WHERE exam_date BETWEEN '2025-12-01' AND '2025-12-31'

question: List the codes of courses whose average score is below 65.
gold_sql: SELECT c.code FROM courses c JOIN marks m ON m.course_id = c.course_id GROUP BY c.course_id, c.code HAVING AVG(m.score) < 65

question: How many male and how many female students does each department have? Show the department name, the gender and the count.
gold_sql: SELECT d.name, s.gender, COUNT(*) FROM students s JOIN departments d ON d.dept_id = s.dept_id GROUP BY d.name, s.gender

question: Which students are not enrolled in any course? Show their first and last names.
gold_sql: SELECT first_name, last_name FROM students s WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM marks m WHERE m.student_id = s.student_id)

question: Which courses have no students enrolled? Give the course code.
gold_sql: SELECT code FROM courses c WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM marks m WHERE m.course_id = c.course_id)

question: List the first and last names of students whose average score is higher than the average of all scores.
gold_sql: SELECT s.first_name, s.last_name FROM students s JOIN marks m ON m.student_id = s.student_id GROUP BY s.student_id, s.first_name, s.last_name HAVING AVG(m.score) > (SELECT AVG(score) FROM marks)

question: For each department, which student in that department has the highest average score? Show the department name and the student's first and last name.
gold_sql: WITH avg_scores AS (SELECT s.student_id, s.first_name, s.last_name, s.dept_id, AVG(m.score) AS avg_score FROM students s JOIN marks m ON m.student_id = s.student_id GROUP BY s.student_id), ranked AS (SELECT *, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY dept_id ORDER BY avg_score DESC) AS rnk FROM avg_scores WHERE avg_score IS NOT NULL) SELECT d.name, r.first_name, r.last_name FROM ranked r JOIN departments d ON d.dept_id = r.dept_id WHERE r.rnk = 1

question: Rank the courses by their average score, where rank 1 is the highest average. Show the course code and its rank, ordered by rank. Only include courses that have marks.
gold_sql: SELECT c.code, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY AVG(m.score) DESC) AS rnk FROM courses c JOIN marks m ON m.course_id = c.course_id GROUP BY c.course_id, c.code ORDER BY rnk

question: Which student or students achieved the highest score in the course titled 'Calculus I'? Show their first and last names.
gold_sql: SELECT s.first_name, s.last_name FROM students s JOIN marks m ON m.student_id = s.student_id JOIN courses c ON c.course_id = m.course_id WHERE c.title = 'Calculus I' AND m.score = (SELECT MAX(m2.score) FROM marks m2 JOIN courses c2 ON c2.course_id = m2.course_id WHERE c2.title = 'Calculus I')

question: List the first and last names of students who are enrolled in courses from at least 3 different departments.
gold_sql: SELECT s.first_name, s.last_name FROM students s JOIN marks m ON m.student_id = s.student_id JOIN courses c ON c.course_id = m.course_id GROUP BY s.student_id, s.first_name, s.last_name HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT c.dept_id) >= 3

question: For each course code, what percentage of its graded marks are 50 or above? Round the percentage to 1 decimal place.
gold_sql: SELECT c.code, ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN m.score >= 50 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(m.score), 1) FROM courses c JOIN marks m ON m.course_id = c.course_id WHERE m.score IS NOT NULL GROUP BY c.course_id, c.code

question: Which students are enrolled in both 'Introduction to Programming' and 'Calculus I'? Show their student_id.
gold_sql: SELECT m.student_id FROM marks m JOIN courses c ON c.course_id = m.course_id WHERE c.title = 'Introduction to Programming' INTERSECT SELECT m.student_id FROM marks m JOIN courses c ON c.course_id = m.course_id WHERE c.title = 'Calculus I'

question: Which department's courses have the highest average score across all their marks? Give the department name.
gold_sql: SELECT d.name FROM departments d JOIN courses c ON c.dept_id = d.dept_id JOIN marks m ON m.course_id = c.course_id GROUP BY d.dept_id, d.name ORDER BY AVG(m.score) DESC LIMIT 1

question: List the first and last names of students who are enrolled in at least one course but in no course offered by the Computer Science department.
gold_sql: SELECT s.first_name, s.last_name FROM students s WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM marks m WHERE m.student_id = s.student_id) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM marks m JOIN courses c ON c.course_id = m.course_id JOIN departments d ON d.dept_id = c.dept_id WHERE m.student_id = s.student_id AND d.name = 'Computer Science')

question: Which instructor has the most enrollments in total across all the courses they teach? Show the instructor and the number of enrollments.
gold_sql: SELECT c.instructor, COUNT(*) AS n FROM courses c JOIN marks m ON m.course_id = c.course_id GROUP BY c.instructor ORDER BY n DESC LIMIT 1

question: On average, how many courses is each enrolled student taking? Round to 2 decimal places.
gold_sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(n), 2) FROM (SELECT student_id, COUNT(*) AS n FROM marks GROUP BY student_id)

question: For every department, show the department name and how many of its students have no email address. Include departments where that number is zero.
gold_sql: SELECT d.name, COUNT(s.student_id) FROM departments d LEFT JOIN students s ON s.dept_id = d.dept_id AND s.email IS NULL GROUP BY d.dept_id, d.name

question: List the first and last names of students who have at least one graded mark and whose graded scores are all 60 or higher.
gold_sql: SELECT s.first_name, s.last_name FROM students s JOIN marks m ON m.student_id = s.student_id WHERE m.score IS NOT NULL GROUP BY s.student_id, s.first_name, s.last_name HAVING MIN(m.score) >= 60
